newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty condemns "appalling" Pakistan human rights.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty condemns "appalling" Pakistan human rights.

text.p: Amnesty International on Tuesday called on the government of Pakistan to reverse an "appalling human rights situation" and accused it of presiding over a culture of violence.

The London-based human rights organisation said elected governments had failed to repair the damage caused by long periods of martial law, during which civil and political rights were suspended, political institutions destroyed and the constitution distorted.

"The majority of Pakistan's people will have little reason to celebrate the country's 50th anniversary on 14 August 1997 as they are still being denied the fundamental human rights guranteed to them by their constitution," Amnesty said in a report.

"Torture, including rape, is widespread in Pakistan. Police often intimidate and humiliate people in custody, beat, kick and use electric shocks on detainees, hang them upside down and deprive them of food and drink," Amnesty said.
"Many people die as a result of torture every year, yet virtually no police have been brought to justice for torturing or killing detainees."
Amnesty cited the case of Yusuf Jakhrani, a politician in his early 40s who died in military custody in 1992 after he was reported to have been tortured for six days.

Amnesty quoted a witness as saying: "His neck was broken...his back appeared to have been roasted and there was a burn and fracture on his right arm. Even his genitals had cigarette burns. It seems that someone had attempted to pull out his fingernails...his nostrils were oozing blood."
Amnesty said the victim's father had pursued the case in vain until 1996 but had given up his struggle as he did not believe justice would ever be done.
Such cases were the rule rather than the exception in Pakistan, Amnesty said.

"Scores of people are extrajudicially executed in Pakistan every year," Amnesty said. "The official story is always that police fired in self-defence, even when their victims have been seen to be arrested, disarmed and handcuffed."
Amnesty called on the government of Pakistan to take human rights seriously.
"This would be not so much a birthday present from the government of Pakistan to the country's people but the final honouring of fundamental rights denied them for 50 years," Amnesty said.
